ig_caption:
The French Defence starts with a quiet move, 1...e6, but it leads to some of the richest games in chess. Here it is at three levels.

At 800: 1...e6 gets ready for ...d5, hitting White's e-pawn. The price is the bishop on c8, which is shut in for now.
At 1200: in the Advance, 3.e5, White builds a pawn chain. Black hits its base on d4 with ...c5, ...Nc6 and ...Qb6.
At 1600: the Winawer, 3...Bb4. Black gives up a bishop to double White's c-pawns.
And if White swaps with 3.exd5 exd5, the c8 bishop is free at last.

slides.title: The French
slides.sub: ONE QUIET MOVE, THREE WAYS TO SEE IT

slides.title: At 800: the idea
slides.take: 1...e6 gets ready for ...d5, and now Black's pawn hits White's e-pawn. Black's pawns are solid and hard to attack.
slides.edge: The price: the bishop on c8 is shut in behind the e6 pawn. Much of the French is about freeing it.

slides.title: At 1200: hit the base
slides.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6
slides.take: White's pawns on d4 and e5 form a chain. Pushing against the front pawn does little. The back pawn, d4, holds it all up.
slides.edge: So Black hits d4 three times: the c5 pawn, the knight on c6 and the queen on b6. The queen also eyes b2.

slides.title: At 1600: the Winawer
slides.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3+ bxc3
slides.take: Black pins the knight, then gives up the bishop for it. White is left with doubled pawns on the c-file.
slides.edge: In return White has two bishops and space. A sharp fight where both sides must know their plans.

slides.title: If White swaps: 3.exd5
slides.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5 exd5
slides.take: The pawns are now even and the same on both sides. It often leads to a calm game.
slides.edge: Good news for Black: the e-pawn has moved, so the c8 bishop is free at last. Develop it before it gets stuck again.
